# stepsecurity_github_pat_exemption (Resource)

Manages one exemption from the PAT governance policy. An exempt token is not evaluated against the policy, receives no pre-expiry reminders and is skipped by every automatic revocation until the exemption expires, after which it re-enters normal enforcement. The exemption names either one token (a classic token by token_suffix, a fine-grained token by token_id) or, with user_login alone, every token of one GitHub user, current and future. It lives in the registry of one organization, or in the tenant-wide registry when organization is omitted. The server removes a record thirty days after it expires; remove the resource from the configuration by then, otherwise Terraform recreates it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    stepsecurity = {
      source = "step-security/stepsecurity"
    }
  }
}

provider "stepsecurity" {
  api_key  = "xxxxxxxx" # can also be set as env variable STEP_SECURITY_API_KEY
  customer = "abcdefg"  # can also be set as env variable STEP_SECURITY_CUSTOMER
}

# Exempt one classic token of an organization until a date, with the change
# record that approved it. The token is named by its last eight characters.
resource "stepsecurity_github_pat_exemption" "release_pipeline_token" {
  organization = "example-org"
  token_suffix = "a1b2c3d4"
  expires_at   = "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z"
  reason       = "Release pipeline token, rotation scheduled for the next quarter"
  record_id    = "CHG0012345"
}

# Exempt a fine-grained token, narrowed to its user. Omitting expires_at lets
# the server set eight days after the approval.
resource "stepsecurity_github_pat_exemption" "deploy_token" {
  organization = "example-org"
  token_id     = 1234567
  user_login   = "deploy-bot"
  reason       = "Deployment automation, replacement in progress"
}

# Tenant-wide: every classic token of one service account, but only on one
# GitHub Enterprise Server. Omit organization for tenant-wide exemptions and
# omit instance to cover every organization of the tenant.
resource "stepsecurity_github_pat_exemption" "service_account" {
  user_login  = "svc-ci"
  token_class = "classic"
  instance    = "ghes.example.com"
  expires_at  = "2027-03-31T00:00:00Z"
  reason      = "Service account tokens are rotated by the platform team"
}

# For importing an existing exemption to terraform state, use organization/key
# as listed by the API, or /key for a tenant-wide exemption.
import {
  to = stepsecurity_github_pat_exemption.release_pipeline_token
  id = "example-org/a1b2c3d4"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the exemption ends, in RFC 3339 form (for example 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z). Omit to let the server set eight days after the approval.
- `instance` (String) Tenant-wide exemptions only: limit the exemption to the organizations of one instance, a GitHub Enterprise Server or data residency server by its registered name, or github.com for GitHub.com organizations. Omit to cover every organization of the tenant.
- `organization` (String) The GitHub organization whose registry holds the exemption. Omit for a tenant-wide exemption, which applies to every organization of the tenant, or to the organizations of one instance when instance is set.
- `reason` (String) Why the exemption was granted, at most 500 characters.
- `record_id` (String) Reference of the approving record, for example a change ticket. Saving an exemption with a record_id replaces any earlier exemption in the same registry that carries the same record_id.
- `source` (String) Name of the approving system, recorded for audit. Defaults to terraform.
- `token_class` (String) For an exemption of every token of a user only: limit it to classic or fine_grained tokens. Omit to cover both classes.
- `token_id` (Number) The id of the fine-grained token to exempt: the token id shown on the Apps & PATs page, or the grant id from the token's URL in the GitHub organization settings.
- `token_suffix` (String) The last eight characters of the classic token to exempt, in lower case (the form the dashboard and the API list).
- `user_login` (String) GitHub login of the token's user. On its own it exempts every token of this user, current and future; together with token_suffix or token_id it narrows the exemption to that user's token.

### Read-Only

- `approved_at` (String) When the exemption was first recorded, in RFC 3339 form.
- `created_by` (String) The principal that recorded the exemption: the API key's identifier, or a user's email.
- `id` (String) The organization and the registry key, as organization/key; a tenant-wide exemption has an empty organization, so its ID starts with a slash.
- `key` (String) The server's registry key for this exemption.
- `scope` (String) token when the exemption names one token, owner when it covers every token of a user.
